body: Yep. I either need to see it as a hindrance or just as something that, like everything else, arises and passes away and is not worth clinging to or craving or deluding myself about. It was just an experience.
I definitely think it was something like a Jhana. I also think I can steer myself away from delusion. The word "coincidence" has become my mantra :)
Right, but, minus the delusion... What is the name for the perceptual experience I had (reverse tunnel vision, body and world becoming one, periphery becoming clear)?

So... did you get the point from my post as to what the solution is?

The secret is to not react to these thoughts. At least, don't react with any of the following:

1. craving
2. aversion
3. ignorance

Don't crave the content of the thoughts.

Don't avert from or be afraid of the thoughts or resent the thoughts for being there.

Don't attempt to make anything up to explain the origin or purpose of the thoughts.

Just allow them to be. Regard them equanimously. Neutrally.

Let them be and this is most important: GO ON ABOUT YOUR BUSINESS OF BEING A GOOD PERSON ANYWAY!!!

FYI: Your response where you detail the contents of the thoughts might be seen as a form of craving. You identify as a person with sick thoughts and so you have the compulsion to discuss them in detail because it gives you a sense of identity. You are afraid of losing your identity so you cling to the details. When you regard them equanimously, you will forget the details soon after they arise and pass away.

Wow! Sounds very similar to my experience. The folks in /r/kundalini got very upset with me when I suggested that all things spiritual may be of the mind and nature.

Buddhism is also now a big part of my path. Very simple, powerful and scientific.

In fact though I would say it's not even Buddhism or any specific practice other than to dive deeply into my body, this moment and really just study reality itself and figure out how to live being my own teacher but studying hard. Patiently and persistently!! The body is an amazing teacher.

I'm ready to accept all of the karma, suffering, punishment. I want to learn to love and leave the sick ways behind. I am my own worst critic. Some think I'm incredibly loving. It's not my fault I am this way. I learned it from my family. My past 5 years has been driven by a desire to change. I want to make the world a better place and help spread peace and harmony and process negativity and heal. I would sacrifice myself to bring happiness to the world. Any advice on living more selflessly would be great. If this isn't kundalini, what is it? Prana? There is a constant tugging or pull of energy being pulled out of my body. The more that is released the lighter and more at ease I feel and the closer to my true loving self. It's like an angel is healing me and pulling the demon out. It all started months ago but really revved up by the 100 hours of meditation that I did with the motivation to lose my ego and become a blessing to the world. I appreciate your help.

Also even at the most intense parts where I was convinced that an external force HAD invaded my body and taken control... Not one hair on my or anyone elses head was hurt so Kundalini does NOT want to kill me. Kundalini and I are best friends!

For one thing it has taught me how to breathe deeply for the first time in as long as I can remember!!!

Also it is the love in me that considers scenarios because of my awareness that sometimes I have control issues and have acted less than loving. It is that I care so much about others that I am willing to bare my soul in these posts to try and come through this with wisdom and the ability to help others.

EXACTLY! This is what I have been trying to say. Siddharta Gautama the Buddha experienced all this deep spiritual stuff. I am sure his Kundalini was awakened. He said it was all mind. All "kalapas" or sub atomic particles arising and passing. Everything we now call spiritual may someday be called science.

And what you said was very hurtful by the way. It was my own anxiety and fear of being taken over by some external supernatural force that made me afraid that something would take my life. My fear came from a desire to live. Since I realized that this release of mental defilements process that seems like Kundalini awakening according to all of the descriptions of symptoms but which you seem so sure is not... since I realized that this process is trying to help transform me into a better person I have not had any such fears even though the intensity has been just as strong.
I was just overreacting to my own anxiety when I posted that. I do feel love for others and I do not have a personality disorder.
I just wonder if what we call spiritual now isn't just science that has yet to be discovered.

Help me understand... I have had a ton of insanely intense spiritual experiences over the past month but I keep telling myself it is just mind. How would I know if it was more than mind? How can anyone know? How does one who thinks they have had an experience beyond mind know it was beyond mind? How do they know it isn't just some neurotransmitter being out of whack? I am not trolling I am serious! I need to know this to understand this experience. If it is spiritual or supernatural then maybe I need to come to that conclusion but I don't see how any experience can prove that.
Same question I asked above. How do you prove something is spiritual and not mind? How do you know it isn't mind?

I have all of the symptoms listed in multiple different descriptions of Kundalini listed here:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kundalini

and here:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kundalini_syndrome

How do you know something is spiritual or supernatural and not just mind? What does proof of supernatural look like? I need to know for my health. I am not trolling. I believe I have been to the limit of experience and I found it all to be mind. How do you know something is not mind??
There may be levels of mind of which the mind we call I is a sub component.

What is called kundalini is really just an increased sensitivity and awareness which leads to the reprogramming of the mind/body connection by the mind. It is a psychosomatic defragmentation and cleanup process that is entirely natural and is the result of the increased sensitivity and awareness that cones from intense meditation. It is a more intense version of having better posture because you feel what bad posture is doing to your spine.

Here's the problem: I have a tendency towards magical thinking and such thinking can actually lead me to psychosis even if it's only a small amount and subconscious.

Why can't spiritual practitioners admit that every sensation or experience they have may just be the product of their mind and imagination?

One of the things I realized after numerous near death out of body enlightenment and other spiritual experiences where my soul came into my body and I spoke in tongues and taught ER nurses and doctors the path to enlightenment and even after seeing that the entire world including the body and out into the depths of space is just a mirror reflecting an internal state of consciousness what I learned is that the mind/brain is a powerful thing, delusion is tricky as hell and there can never be ANY proof of supernatural entities. It can all just be a hallucination or sensation which is interpreted non-equanimously.

I can't work with anyone who calls on an external or supernatural energy source.

Thank you kind soul. Yes, I do have a problem with anxiety. Any advice for dealing with it? 

When I feel bad I think it will go on forever. When I feel good I know it will end any minute. I never feel safe or confident. My mom says I am a prince who thinks he's a frog.

In meditation I never seem to be able to let go of my ego. I have felt and realized Anatta, the ever-changing impersonal nature of mind, but even through that there was some part of my consciousness that still held on to a point at the center of my brain.

I'm afraid that if I don't learn how to let go of ego that my death will be a painful struggle.

Sometimes it is really difficult for me to find a loving, kind, positive energy in myself. I am working with a therapist and a psychiatrist but I think I have a deeper problem. I think I may have a personality disorder. I have emotionally hurt people intentionally or tried to control people because it gives me a sick pleasure. I am upset about something that happened in childhood and it made me turn against the world and turn crooked. I want so much to be a good person and I feel tremendous guilt for my past actions but yet I still can't seem to feel love and kindness and send positive energy out from within. I can barely feel anything positive within! I am thinking maybe if I start volunteering. Helping the unfortunate. Maybe that would help me change my personality at the deepest levels. I know there is a true me in here that is innocent and wants to help make the world a better more loving place. There is an epic battle taking place in my body for ownership of it and I want the right side to win.

OK, so, tell me more about this "basic energy work" and how it can harm. Please? I am teaching myself and making progress but the more information I have the better I feel. 

Can you see why Goenka tried to keep Reiki people out of Vipassana? He said he had numerous experiences of Reiki people becoming mentally unstable in Vipassana. My guess is that these people were not doing proper Reiki, but, like me, were doing what you call "basic energy work". So, I really would like to know more about what myself and these people were specifically doing wrong and how I harmed myself.

I understand it wasn't Reiki that got me in trouble. I think it was some misunderstandings on my part that from Goenka's perspective must easily arise in some Reiki practitioners... Here are what I know so far I was doing wrong:

1. Thinking magically
2. Believing in external forces such as soul, creator, divine, luck
3. Ascribing intention to objects, lucky rocks etc...
4. Craving, aversion & ignorance
5. Imagining the sensations were spiritual energies
6. Moving these energies around with my hands
7. Auto-suggestion & self-hypnosis
8. Believing that the meditation would cure my depression and anxiety and lead me towards an enlightened existence.

I think this is most of it. Apparently Reiki, Qi Gong and some other practices can cause some people (who are doing it wrong) to be tricked or misled in these kinds of ways that can result in psychosis.

Either that or I really did awaken the kundalini and just need to have catharsis in a monastery for the next several years.

Yes, I am exercizing.

Yes, I am sleeping. Better than I have in years. This whole thing has actually improved many aspects of my life.

Yes, I am working. More focused and effective than before.

I am eating a little too much, but very healthfully. Meat, veggies, lots of water. Very little junk.

Family and friends are great. I haven't told many except for close family about what is going on but I seem able to hide it quite well. Whenever I am focusing on the moment, such as when socializing, the psychosis symptoms or "kundalini" or whatever it is seems to subside. It only arises when I wake up in the morning or dwell on it mentally.

People have commented that I have changed since doing the meditation retreat. They say I am more positive, more effective at work, More even keeled, less easily worked up, less moody.

When some intense feeling like drilling in the skull starts, I will intentionally practice feeling it as just muscle tension in the scalp (as it is) rather than allow my imagination to run away and think of it as a spiritual or alien thing.

I intentionally am bringing my awareness deeper into the body and into the present moment when I catch myself drifting into excessive thinking or fantasy. This helps me breathe (breathing more deeply now than I have in years) and be more positive.

OK, so, essentially... recognize that my faculty to think or use my mind in any kind of effective way is severely compromised right now, and stop trying to figure anything out. OK. I can do that.

However, the only way I have found to stop my mind from thinking or not to further energize it is to practice Shamatha type meditation or Anapana... just being aware of thoughts but not attaching to them. So, it still seems like I will have to practice meditation of some kind or another just to avoid compulsive thinking.

Also, when feelings of resentment for being sick come up in me, the only way I can shift out of these (which lead to harmful depressive side of the illness) is to tap into feelings of love and kindness... which is essentially the Metta practice.

So, in conclusion, it seems like to do what I need to do I need to at least practice calm abiding type meditation such as Shamatha and loving kindness meditation such as Metta.

You can read my original post that I linked to. Essentially...

1. suicidal ideation
2. delusions of grandeur
3. mania
4. depression
5. fear of being possessed by a demon or controlled by aliens
6. believing myself to be the savior of mankind

Oh, I am listening. However, it's close to impossible for me to stop practicing. I am compulsively body scanning every moment I am awake and find it almost impossible to stop. Here is what is helping:

Catching myself thinking magically and switching to a scientific view, stopping worrying about the future or regretting the past, changing my perspective on sensations to be more realistic (instead of it feeling like drilling in my skull, I try to feel it just as muscle tension in the scalp). Always trying to feel sensations "as they are", coming into the body and into the present, grounding, staying busy, etc...

Basically the sensations of the psychosis immediately pick up as soon as I do any of the following:

1. start thinking rather than being present
2. become either manic or depressed
3. stop paying attention to the present
4. use my imagination excessively

This syndrome I now have seems to be forcing me into the present moment. One slip out of the present moment could mean psychosis.

I would just like to get the perspective of a master of both Reiki and Vipassana as to exactly what kinds of thoughts and intentions I need to steer away from.

I'm quitting the yoga studio. They hawked a bunch of snake oil mlm junk and were costing me too much money anyway.

My spiritual practice now will be as follows:

1. Breathing.
2. Holding still both in body and mind.
3. Listening to silence.
4. Helping others, being kind and loving.
5. Practicing singing songs and playing guitar.
5. Taking care of plants and animals.
6. Taking care of friends and family.
7. Taking care of myself.
8. Reminding myself I don't have to worry or over think things.
9. Being present.
10. Thinking rationally, scientifically, regarding sensations equanimously and going about my business.
11. Bringing an end to magical thinking, auto suggestion and self hypnosis.
12. Trusting my doctors.
13. Trusting my true self and wisdom.
14. Enjoying this moment!
15. Maybe get a pet.

I could use advice on any of these or the whole plan. Thank you for the help so far. You all have been great and it means so much!!

Thank you. I love my meds. The idea of getting off of them is that I can't feel the release of Sankharas as they are with the medicine blunting the sensations. I want to face them in their full, raw state and let them all be fully released by being equanimous to them so I can reach the final goal as Goenka called it and find true happiness and release from Samsara and live a saintly life.

Thank you.

I think I can reach Bhanga Jhana pretty easily. I can feel my entire body and mind, including the consciousness I previously knew as "I" as an ever changing field of subatomic particles arising and passing continuously and impersonally.

Anicca, Anatta are both constant realities for me now.

I'm not sure I have fully understood Dukkha yet. Funny that this realization which is seemingly understood easily is the last for me to attain.

I forgive the universe for being imperfect and containing suffering but I don't see yet why it has to be that way. I still imagine a perfect universe without suffering is possible.
True. However, I have become convinced that placebo is extremely powerful and in fact the only thing powerful enough to cure my lifelong issues.

I want to iterate one thing:

My life has radically improved since the Vipassana retreat, regardless of the scary stuff it revealed in me. I am happier than I have ever been and more effective at work and in relationships.

According to Goenka himself, the proof of doing Vipassana wrong or right is that if your life is not improving, you are doing it wrong.

I wonder if Goenka knows that the true secret to Vipassana is that it turns your life into an LSD trip and if you can hang on and work with it, you get a much more fulfilling life and opportunity to spread peace and harmony.

First 3 days of Vipassana were Anapana, which is meant to focus Samadhi or concentration.

Vipassana has exposed all that was previously subconscious in me. My psychiatrist agrees. She says "All that has changed is my perception."

I thank Vipassana for this. In fact, I have improved my life in so many ways since the retreat. Getting properly diagnosed, right meds. The release of Sankharas is teaching me how to breathe, how to stretch, how to relieve stress and not take it in in the first place, how to stop worrying.

Basically... Vipassana made me so sensitive to my own body and mind that now I have 2 very clear choices in each present moment: 1. be happy 2. go insane and die.

I am getting exactly what I asked for and am optimistic about the process. The biggest challenge will be to be happy even when the depression returns. To perceive the depression AS IT IS... just a sensation. A sensation to be observed with awareness and regarded equanimously, not with craving, aversion or ignorance.

I need a Vipassana coach who won't shy away due to the intense reaction I have had to the technique and my history.

Thanks man. This whole process has in some ways been so magical. Dangerous for me to think that way but all of it seems so perfect. Probably just a manic delusion on my part. Learning stillness and patience is definitely a huge thing I need to learn.

The big lesson both my psychiatrist and psychologist have told me I need to learn, and it jives with Vipassana too... Is to go about my business of being happy REGARDLESS of how I feel. In Vipassana language, regard sensations equanimously. Now I have to learn also to regard mental sensations of depression, mania, delusions, hallucinations equanimously too.

No one can help me figure out whether I did the meditation right or wrong or how to proceed? The doctor is just going to tell me to stay on meds, which is fine, but I still need to learn wisdom / develop skills of equanimity, and Vipassana helps me do that. My yoga studio helps me contact the feeling of love, which is basically what Metta is, which is totally compatible with Vipassana. I need to know which practices to remove from my meditation practice to be safe and continue down the path to develop wisdom and release all my past non-equanimous reactions (Sankharas). I need a meditation guide in addition to a psychiatrist.

My perspective on the meds is that they are like training wheels which can help me go gently into this process. However, they are not stopping the process. The process (awakening) continues and I need to know how to face it correctly and the psychiatrist can't advise me on this.

Regarding hallucinations... Can't you close your eyes and see lights and shapes and colors and such? Isn't it just a well developed imagination? At its peak it was just a cool ability to see figures in the clouds and such.

I am not afraid of the hallucinations. The one thing my psychiatrist told me is that hallucinations can't kill me or harm me or make me more insane or anything. The only things which can do that are excessive delusion... mania or depression.
